title: Absolute area under a scaled Brownian motion with resetting
abstract: We investigate the statistical properties and ergodic behavior of the absolute area below the trajectory of a particle subject to stochastic resetting and moving according to a scaled Brownian motion with exponent $β$. We compare the contributions to the absolute area from the waiting times between resets and the backward recurrence time. Using the renewal formalism we derive the lower-order moments of the absolute area under both Poissonian and heavy-tailed power-law resetting waiting time distributions with exponent $α$. For Poissonian resetting, stochastic interruption suppresses fluctuations, driving the area to be ergodic, regardless of the value of $β$. In contrast, power-law resetting yields a rich spectrum of ergodic regimes. For $0 < α< 1$, the system displays weak ergodicity breaking and the maximum contribution dominates the area accumulated during the waiting times. For $1+β< α< 2$, we unveil an ergodic transition exclusive to the subdiffusive regime at $α=1+β$, where ergodicity is restored. These results clarify the subtle interplay between anomalous diffusion and power-law waiting times between resettings. Our results are tested by numerical simulations exhibiting an excellent agreement.
summary: This work analyzes how stochastic resetting affects the accumulated absolute area of a particle undergoing anomalous diffusion. Using renewal theory, the authors distinguish between Poissonian and heavy-tailed power-law resetting. They find that while Poissonian resetting always restores ergodicity, power-law resetting leads to complex non-ergodic behavior, predicting a specific ergodic transition only when the system is subdiffusive.
main_problem: The study investigates the statistical properties and ergodic behavior of the absolute area accumulated under the trajectory of a particle undergoing stochastic resetting while moving via a scaled Brownian motion.
main_result: The paper reveals that Poissonian resetting always restores ergodicity, whereas power-law resetting exhibits complex regimes, including weak ergodicity breaking and a specific ergodic transition occurring only in the subdiffusive regime at $\alpha = 1+\beta$.
method: The analysis employs the renewal formalism and Laplace transforms to derive the lower-order moments of the absolute area, decomposing the total area into contributions from waiting times and recurrence times.
model_or_system: The model involves a particle subject to a scaled Brownian motion (SBM) characterized by exponent $\beta$, interrupted by stochastic resetting events governed by a waiting time distribution with power-law exponent $\alpha$.
key_observables: Absolute area under the trajectory ($Z_r(t)$), lower-order moments of the area, and the ergodicity breaking parameter (EB).
important_parameters: Anomalous diffusion exponent $\beta$ (for SBM) and power-law resetting exponent $\alpha$ (for waiting times).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the renewal formalism and the ability to calculate moments via Laplace transforms, often focusing on the first two moments to diagnose ergodicity.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate the absolute area decomposition and plot the time evolution of the first two moments and the EB parameter, showing theoretical predictions matching simulations.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework using the renewal formalism, analyzes the contributions of different area components ($	ext{A}_{	ext{N}}$, $	ext{A}_{	ext{back}}$, $	ext{A}_{	ext{max}}$), and then derives specific results for Poissonian versus power-law resetting regimes, culminating in the identification of the ergodic transition point.
why_interesting: The interplay between anomalous diffusion (governed by $\beta$) and non-Markovian memory effects (governed by $\alpha$) in determining the long-term statistical behavior (ergodicity) is a rich topic relevant to non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
